It names Donald Menzel as a rumored MJ-12 member, gives 1947 onward instead of 1952, and leaves out the Eisenhower briefing. It also stresses what the document would prove if it is real: that a saucer crashed and the wreckage was recovered.

plain: A secret paper is said to have briefed Dwight Eisenhower, then president-elect, in 1952 that a flying saucer had crashed and the government had its wreckage. Michels tells it himself, calling it "easily the most controversial" document "in UFO circles" and describing it as "supposedly a briefing document prepared in 1952". The paper is tied to Majestic 12, said to be a secret group of officials set up under President Harry Truman to handle the matter. In another telling Michels relays the view of the UFO researcher Stanton Friedman: if it is a "legitimate document", it shows first "that a flying saucer crashed" and second "that the wreckage was recovered". That version stretches from 1947 onward and names a man named Donald Menzel as a rumored member of the group. A researcher who goes by the online name UAPGerb also tells it, saying "I'm particularly fond of the Eisenhower briefing document." He places it between 1947 and 1952 and links it to Truman, Eisenhower, the defense official James Forrestal and a man named Walter B. Smith.
